sourcesConsulted: model knowledge of the falls prevention literature
gradeRationale: These are leads only; certainty needs retrieved and inspected records.
synthesis: The recorded search failed, so these five items are leads recalled by the model to help build a better query. They suggest that reminders and peer contact may improve attendance and home exercise, but none has been retrieved or checked.

items.title: Reminder messages and attendance at exercise programmes for older adults: an overview of trials
items.keyFindings: Reminder messages were associated with modestly higher attendance in several small trials.

items.title: Peer mentoring to sustain exercise after falls prevention classes
items.keyFindings: Former participants acting as mentors kept contact with most new participants for three months.

items.title: Home exercise calendars and adherence among older adults after group exercise
items.keyFindings: A tick calendar reviewed by the instructor was linked to more days of home exercise.

items.title: Transport support and attendance at community exercise classes for older people
items.keyFindings: Free transport raised attendance among people without a car.

items.title: Behaviour change techniques for exercise adherence in later life
items.keyFindings: Self-monitoring and feedback were the techniques most often linked to adherence.

summary: Five leads after a failed search; no certainty.
